column1: # Authoritative coordinates for localities whose recorded isolate coordinates
# contradict the place their label names.
# build_lat_longs.py normally positions a locality at the mean of its isolates'
# recorded coordinates, which is correct for the great majority of this dataset.
# The entries below are the exceptions: localities where the metadata's own
# Latitude/Longitude are wrong (transposed digits, a dropped minus sign) or
# where a batch of isolates carries a different place's centroid. The country
# and city labels are treated as authoritative, so the named place wins and the
# Anchoring a city is enough to fix its country and region too: an anchored
# isolate contributes the anchor position to those rollups as well.

column5: Trujillo, Venezuela. 7 isolates record latitude 90.42 for 9.42; 90+ is not a valid latitude.
Guangdong, China. 8 isolates record longitude 133.25 for 113.25; agrees with the one GIS-exact isolate at 23.117/113.250.
State of Iowa centroid. One isolate (TgCyW6) drops the minus from its longitude, placing it in China.
Nicaragua. One isolate of two (TgCkNi45) drops the minus from its longitude, placing it in the Gulf of Guinea.
State of Ceara, Brazil. 3 of 6 isolates carry Parana coordinates ~1200 km away.
State of Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil. 1 of 4 isolates carries Minas Gerais coordinates.
Commonwealth of Massachusetts centroid. 29 of 82 isolates carry Pennsylvania coordinates; the label is treated as authoritative.
State of Minnesota centroid. Sampling legitimately spans 2.3 degrees, so the mean is fine but the anchor keeps it off the validator's spread check.
Vancouver, British Columbia. TgCgCa2(nd) drops the minus from its longitude, placing it in northeastern China. Sign-corrected; the row is GIS-exact, so its precision is kept.
Figueira da Foz, Portugal. TgCkPr1 drops the minus from its longitude, placing it in Sardinia. Sign-corrected; the row is GIS-exact, so its precision is kept.
